title: Japan's crypto-exchange registration regime takes effect
summary: Amendments to Japan's Payment Services Act introduced a registration and consumer-protection regime for cryptocurrency exchanges.
details: The law defined virtual currencies for regulatory purposes and required domestic exchange operators to register with the Financial Services Agency. It also imposed anti-money-laundering, identity-verification, disclosure, and customer-asset segregation duties.
whyItMatters: Japan became one of the first major economies to place Bitcoin exchange services inside a national licensing framework.

title: Industry companies announce the New York Agreement
summary: A group of Bitcoin businesses and miners backed a compromise combining SegWit activation with a later block-size increase.
details: The agreement, commonly called SegWit2x, sought to end a long-running dispute over transaction capacity. It was influential but was not a consensus change adopted through Bitcoin Core's normal review process.
whyItMatters: The agreement exposed the limits of company and miner coordination when node operators and developers did not share the same plan.

title: Binance launches
summary: An exchange founded weeks before China's crackdown grew into the largest venue in the market.
details: Operating without a declared headquarters, it served users in jurisdictions where it held no licence and reached dominant share of global spot and derivatives volume. Its founder later pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an anti-money-laundering programme.
whyItMatters: For most of the following decade, the single largest venue setting bitcoin's price was one no regulator clearly supervised.

title: BTC-e is taken offline as U.S. charges are unsealed
summary: U.S. authorities charged BTC-e and alleged operator Alexander Vinnik after the exchange was disrupted by law enforcement.
details: The indictment alleged that the exchange operated an unlicensed money-service business and processed criminal proceeds, including funds linked to the Mt. Gox theft. The allegations were charges at the time and were not themselves a final adjudication of every asserted fact.
whyItMatters: The case demonstrated that long-running Bitcoin exchanges could be reached through cross-border financial-crime enforcement.

sources.title: Russian National and Bitcoin Exchange Charged in 21-Count Indictment

title: A user-activated soft fork forces SegWit's hand
summary: BIP 148 nodes began rejecting blocks that did not signal support for Segregated Witness.
details: After miners had declined to signal for months, the proposal moved the decision to the economic nodes: run this software and blocks that ignore SegWit stop counting for you. Faced with a possible chain split, miners activated SegWit through a competing mechanism days earlier, so BIP 148 never had to orphan anything.
whyItMatters: It established that miners do not decide Bitcoin's rules on their own, which is the constitutional question the whole scaling war was really about.
technicalNote: BIP 148 required blocks after 1 August 2017 to signal bit 1. Miners instead locked in SegWit through BIP 91, which reached threshold in late July and made the split moot.

sources.title: BIP 148: Mandatory activation of segwit deployment

title: Bitcoin Cash splits from Bitcoin
summary: A group favoring larger on-chain blocks launched Bitcoin Cash through an incompatible fork of Bitcoin's transaction history.
details: The new network raised its block-size limit and created a separate asset for holders at the split. Bitcoin nodes that did not adopt those rules continued on the original consensus chain.
whyItMatters: The split turned the scaling debate into two independently traded networks and clarified that incompatible rule changes can create new assets rather than overwrite Bitcoin.
technicalNote: Bitcoin Cash diverged after block 478558 and adopted consensus rules incompatible with Bitcoin.

title: Segregated Witness locks in
summary: Miner signaling reached the threshold that locked in Segregated Witness for activation during the next difficulty period.
details: SegWit changed how transaction signatures are committed and measured while retaining compatibility for older nodes. Lock-in followed years of engineering work and a contentious debate over scaling and activation methods.
whyItMatters: Lock-in made activation of Bitcoin's most substantial capacity and malleability upgrade since its early years effectively certain.
technicalNote: Lock-in occurred at block 479,707 on 8 August 2017 UTC. Contemporaneous coverage often reports 9 August because the block landed late in the UTC day.

title: Segregated Witness activates on Bitcoin
summary: SegWit activated at block 481824, introducing a new transaction format and effective block-weight system.
details: The soft fork fixed third-party transaction malleability for SegWit spends and separated signature data into a witness structure. It also enabled safer construction of layered protocols such as the Lightning Network.
whyItMatters: SegWit expanded practical transaction capacity and supplied key foundations for Bitcoin's next generation of wallets and payment channels.
technicalNote: Activation used BIP9 version-bit signaling and began enforcement at height 481824.

title: Chinese regulators prohibit token fundraising
summary: Seven Chinese agencies declared initial coin offerings unauthorized and ordered fundraising activity to stop.
details: The notice primarily addressed token sales rather than Bitcoin's protocol, but it marked a broad tightening of China's digital-asset policy. Authorities subsequently intensified pressure on domestic trading venues.
whyItMatters: The action began a multi-stage retreat of a once-dominant Bitcoin trading market from mainland China.

title: Major mainland Chinese exchanges announce closures
summary: BTCC and other large platforms moved to end yuan-denominated trading after direction from Chinese authorities.
details: The closures displaced a market that had previously reported a large share of global Bitcoin volume. Trading demand moved toward offshore venues, over-the-counter markets, and stablecoin pairs.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin liquidity proved able to migrate across borders even as a major national market closed centralized trading channels.

sources.title: China Bitcoin Exchange to Stop Trading Virtual Currencies

title: SegWit2x organizers cancel the planned hard fork
summary: Backers of SegWit2x suspended its two-megabyte hard fork after concluding that the change lacked sufficient consensus.
details: The proposal had support from several large miners and companies but faced sustained opposition from many users and Bitcoin Core contributors. Its cancellation avoided an imminent chain split under the SegWit2x schedule.
whyItMatters: The outcome became a defining example of Bitcoin governance extending beyond hash power and corporate coordination.

title: Steam stops accepting bitcoin
summary: Valve removed bitcoin payments, citing high fees and price volatility during the transaction window.
details: Fees had risen to several dollars per transaction and the price could move materially between checkout and confirmation, leaving customers under- or over-paid. Valve had accepted bitcoin for twenty months.
whyItMatters: It is the clearest case of the fee market pricing out exactly the everyday commerce bitcoin was first pitched for.

title: Cboe launches regulated Bitcoin futures
summary: Cboe Futures Exchange opened trading in cash-settled Bitcoin futures under the ticker XBT.
details: The product used a reference price from the Gemini exchange and operated within a U.S. regulated derivatives venue. Heavy initial interest briefly strained Cboe's website.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin gained its first futures contract on a major U.S. regulated exchange.

sources.title: Cboe Announces Bitcoin Futures to Start Trading Sunday

title: Bitcoin peaks near $20,000
summary: The 2017 rally topped out just under $20,000 before losing more than four fifths of its value.
details: The run had drawn retail attention worldwide, futures listings on two U.S. exchanges, and a fee market that made small payments uneconomic. Bitcoin would not trade at this level again for three years.
whyItMatters: It set the template later cycles were measured against: a parabolic top, a long drawdown, and a recovery that outlasts the people who called it dead.
technicalNote: Quoted peaks differ by venue and index; figures near $19,800 are commonly cited for 17 December 2017.

title: CME launches cash-settled Bitcoin futures
summary: CME Group began trading a cash-settled Bitcoin futures contract based on its regulated reference rate.
details: Each contract represented five bitcoin and settled to the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate. The launch brought Bitcoin risk management to one of the world's largest derivatives marketplaces.
whyItMatters: CME futures became a durable institutional market and later an important reference point in U.S. Bitcoin ETP decisions.

sources.title: CME Group Self-Certifies Bitcoin Futures to Launch Dec. 18

title: Coincheck discloses a major exchange theft
summary: Japanese exchange Coincheck halted withdrawals after attackers stole a large quantity of NEM tokens from a hot wallet.
details: The stolen asset was not bitcoin, but the failure affected confidence and oversight across Japan's cryptocurrency market. Coincheck later pledged customer reimbursement and faced regulatory orders to improve controls.
whyItMatters: The incident accelerated Japan's move from early licensing toward more demanding exchange supervision.

sources.title: Japan's Coincheck says $534 million in cryptocurrency stolen

title: Lightning Labs releases the first lnd mainnet beta
summary: Lightning Labs released lnd 0.4-beta with support for real-value channels on Bitcoin mainnet.
details: The team aimed the release at developers, technical users, and routing-node operators and advised using small amounts. It included cross-implementation support, safer seed handling, and improved pathfinding.
whyItMatters: The release marked the Lightning Network's transition from experiments toward a usable public payment network.

sources.title: Announcing Our First Lightning Mainnet Release, lnd 0.4-beta

technicalNote: Lightning channels use Bitcoin transactions and hashed timelock contracts to settle off-chain payment updates.

title: Mt. Gox enters civil rehabilitation
summary: A Tokyo court approved the start of civil rehabilitation proceedings for the failed Mt. Gox exchange.
details: The change replaced the prior bankruptcy process and allowed creditor claims to be valued under a rehabilitation plan. It opened a path for some distributions in bitcoin and bitcoin cash rather than treating every claim only at old yen values.
whyItMatters: The ruling established the legal process that eventually returned assets to some creditors six years later.

sources.title: Order of Commencement of Civil Rehabilitation Proceedings

title: SEC again rejects the Winklevoss Bitcoin trust listing
summary: The SEC disapproved a proposed exchange rule change for the Winklevoss Bitcoin Trust, citing market-surveillance concerns.
details: The decision focused on whether the listing exchange could prevent fraudulent and manipulative practices in underlying spot markets. Commissioner Hester Peirce issued a public dissent.
whyItMatters: The order framed the surveillance test that shaped years of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETP litigation and filings.

title: Intercontinental Exchange announces Bakkt
summary: ICE announced Bakkt as a regulated digital-asset platform built with major technology and retail partners.
details: The plan included physically delivered Bitcoin futures, custody, and merchant applications. Regulatory work delayed the futures launch until the following year.
whyItMatters: A leading global exchange operator committed to building institutional Bitcoin trading and custody infrastructure.

title: A bug that could have printed bitcoin is quietly patched
summary: Bitcoin Core 0.16.3 fixed a flaw that allowed both a crash and, in some versions, the creation of coins from nothing.
details: CVE-2018-17144 let a miner construct a block spending the same output twice; affected nodes would either crash or, in versions from 0.15.0, accept the block and inflate the supply. It was disclosed privately, patched, and only then described in full.
whyItMatters: The most serious bug found in Bitcoin since 2010 was caught before anyone exploited it, and the handling became the template for later disclosures.
technicalNote: The duplicate-input check had been moved for performance in 0.14.0, leaving the case unhandled. No exploiting block was ever mined.

title: Blockstream launches the Liquid sidechain
summary: Blockstream put Liquid into production as a federated Bitcoin sidechain for exchanges and trading firms.
details: Liquid enabled faster inter-exchange settlement and issued assets through a federation rather than Bitcoin's permissionless mining model. Users peg bitcoin into L-BTC through the federation and later redeem it back to the base chain.
whyItMatters: Liquid became a prominent example of extending Bitcoin with a separate trust and performance model.
technicalNote: Liquid uses a strong federation and one-minute blocks; it is not secured by Bitcoin proof of work in the same way as the base chain.

title: Bitcoin Cash divides into BCH and Bitcoin SV
summary: Competing rule sets produced a contentious split of the Bitcoin Cash network into BCH and Bitcoin SV.
details: The dispute involved incompatible changes and rival mining campaigns, sometimes described as a hash war. Bitcoin itself did not fork during this event, but exchanges and wallet providers had to manage operational and naming risks.
whyItMatters: The episode illustrated the continuing ecosystem costs of contentious forks and concentrated mining coordination.

sources.title: Bitcoin Cash Hard Fork Creates Two New Blockchains

title: The 2018 bear market bottoms near $3,200
summary: Bitcoin reached the low of its post-2017 decline, down roughly 84% from the peak.
details: The drawdown had run for a year and taken most of the initial-coin-offering market with it. Development, mining and institutional groundwork continued through it largely unremarked.
whyItMatters: The archive records tops readily and bottoms rarely, though the bottoms are where most of the building happens.

title: The Lightning Torch begins its global relay
summary: A pseudonymous user started a Lightning payment relay in which each participant added satoshis before forwarding it.
details: The experiment moved through users, developers, executives, and public figures across many countries. It demonstrated interoperable Lightning payments while the network was still small and experimental.
whyItMatters: The relay gave Lightning an accessible public demonstration and a memorable early culture event.

sources.title: Bitcoin's Lightning Torch Has Been Passed Around the World

title: QuadrigaCX enters creditor protection
summary: A Canadian court granted creditor protection to QuadrigaCX after the exchange said it could not access substantial customer assets.
details: Proceedings followed the reported death of founder Gerald Cotten, who was said to control key wallet credentials. Later investigations found severe recordkeeping failures and extensive misuse of customer funds.
whyItMatters: QuadrigaCX became a major warning about opaque custody, key-person risk, and the absence of verifiable reserves.

sources.title: Quadriga Fintech Solutions Corp. Case Documents

title: Fidelity Digital Assets begins service rollout
summary: Fidelity began rolling out Bitcoin custody and trade-execution services to selected institutional clients.
details: The service separated custody from exchange execution and drew on Fidelity's existing institutional operations. Access expanded gradually rather than through a single retail launch.
whyItMatters: A large traditional asset manager brought its brand and operational infrastructure directly into institutional Bitcoin custody.

sources.title: Fidelity's New Cryptocurrency Company Is Up and Running

title: Cboe stops listing new Bitcoin futures contracts
summary: Cboe Futures Exchange said it would not add a new XBT Bitcoin futures contract while reviewing its approach.
details: Existing contracts remained available until their final expirations. CME's competing futures market continued and later became the dominant regulated U.S. venue for Bitcoin derivatives.
whyItMatters: The withdrawal showed that regulated product launches did not guarantee lasting liquidity or market share.

sources.title: CFE Product Update: Cboe Bitcoin Futures

title: Binance reports a 7,000 BTC hot-wallet theft
summary: Binance disclosed that attackers withdrew 7,000 BTC from one of its hot wallets in a coordinated security breach.
details: The exchange paused deposits and withdrawals while investigating and covered the loss through its emergency insurance fund. Bitcoin's base protocol was not compromised.
whyItMatters: The theft reinforced the distinction between Bitcoin network security and the operational security of custodial exchanges.

title: The PlusToken scheme collapses
summary: One of the largest cryptocurrency Ponzi schemes on record stopped paying out, having taken in billions.
details: The operation promised high returns on deposits and recruited heavily across China and South Korea. Chinese authorities prosecuted dozens of participants, and movements of the seized coins were widely blamed for pressuring the market.
whyItMatters: It showed that fraud at national scale could distort bitcoin's price long after the fraud itself had stopped.

title: FATF applies global standards to virtual-asset providers
summary: The Financial Action Task Force adopted guidance applying anti-money-laundering standards, including transfer information duties, to virtual-asset service providers.
details: The Interpretive Note to Recommendation 15 required jurisdictions to license or register covered providers and supervise them for AML compliance. Its transfer-data requirement became widely known as the crypto Travel Rule.
whyItMatters: The guidance created a common international compliance baseline for Bitcoin exchanges and custodians.

sources.title: Public Statement on Virtual Assets and Related Providers

title: Bakkt launches physically delivered Bitcoin futures
summary: Bakkt opened trading in daily and monthly Bitcoin futures that settled through delivery of bitcoin held in regulated custody.
details: The contracts traded on ICE Futures U.S. and cleared through ICE Clear US. Early volumes were modest, but the product broadened regulated institutional market structure.
whyItMatters: Bakkt linked futures, clearing, and custody in a major exchange group's Bitcoin product.

title: UNICEF launches a cryptocurrency-denominated fund
summary: UNICEF announced a fund able to receive, hold, and disburse donations in bitcoin and ether without converting them first.
details: The fund's first contribution came from the Ethereum Foundation and supported open-source technology projects. Bitcoin donations were handled as bitcoin, providing transparent asset-denominated accounting.
whyItMatters: A United Nations organization incorporated native cryptocurrency donations into its formal funding operations.

title: Germany creates a regulated crypto-custody service category
summary: German lawmakers approved legislation bringing crypto custody into the country's regulated financial-services framework.
details: The law required firms providing custody of cryptographic keys as a business to obtain authorization from BaFin. Transitional provisions allowed existing operators time to signal and complete applications.
whyItMatters: A major European economy created a direct legal path for supervised Bitcoin custody providers.

sources.title: Guidance Notice on Crypto Custody Business

title: CME launches options on Bitcoin futures
summary: CME Group introduced regulated options based on its established Bitcoin futures contract.
details: The options were quoted in U.S. dollars and settled into CME Bitcoin futures. They gave institutional participants another tool for hedging volatility and expressing time-bounded market views.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin's regulated derivatives market expanded beyond linear futures into a conventional options structure.

title: The Taproot proposals are published
summary: BIPs 340, 341 and 342 set out Schnorr signatures, Taproot outputs and a new scripting version.
details: Schnorr signatures allow several signers to produce one signature, and Taproot lets a complex spending policy look identical on-chain to an ordinary payment when everyone cooperates. Together they improve both privacy and the cost of multi-party contracts.
whyItMatters: This is the design that became Bitcoin's most recent consensus change, and the basis of most contract work since.

sources.title: BIP 341: Taproot — SegWit version 1 spending rules

title: India's Supreme Court strikes down the crypto banking ban
summary: The court held that the central bank's order cutting exchanges off from banking was disproportionate.
details: The Reserve Bank of India had in 2018 forbidden regulated banks from serving cryptocurrency businesses, which effectively closed the domestic market. The judgment restored banking access while leaving the government free to legislate.
whyItMatters: It reopened one of the world's largest potential user bases, and set an early precedent that a regulator cannot ban an asset by cutting its plumbing.
actors: Internet and Mobile Association of India

sources.title: Internet and Mobile Association of India v. Reserve Bank of India

title: Bitcoin plunges during the global pandemic sell-off
summary: Bitcoin fell roughly 40 percent intraday as global markets rushed toward cash during the early COVID-19 shock.
details: The move triggered large leveraged liquidations and stressed several cryptocurrency trading venues. Bitcoin's network continued producing blocks, while the market episode challenged its short-term safe-haven narrative.
whyItMatters: The crash became Bitcoin's sharpest modern liquidity stress test and a reference point for later market-risk controls.

sources.title: Bitcoin Price Plunges as Global Markets Fall

title: Bitcoin's third halving reduces the subsidy to 6.25 BTC
summary: Block 630000 cut Bitcoin's per-block subsidy from 12.5 BTC to 6.25 BTC.
details: The programmed event reduced the flow of newly issued bitcoin by half without changing the 21 million maximum supply. Miners continued to earn transaction fees in addition to the smaller subsidy.
whyItMatters: The third halving reaffirmed Bitcoin's predictable issuance schedule through another full four-year epoch.
technicalNote: The consensus subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks.

title: Hijacked Twitter accounts run a bitcoin scam
summary: Attackers took over verified accounts belonging to major public figures and posted a doubling scam.
details: The accounts of Barack Obama, Elon Musk, Apple and others promised to return double any bitcoin sent to a given address. The take was modest, but the compromise reached an internal Twitter administration tool.
whyItMatters: It gave bitcoin its widest mainstream exposure that year in the worst possible framing, and hardened the association with fraud.

sources.title: An update on our security incident

title: OCC confirms U.S. national banks may custody crypto assets
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said national banks and federal thrifts may provide cryptocurrency custody services.
details: Interpretive Letter 1170 treated safekeeping of cryptographic keys as a modern form of traditional custody. Banks still had to manage operational, compliance, and security risks under existing law.
whyItMatters: The letter gave federally chartered banks a clear legal basis to enter Bitcoin custody.
actors: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: Federally Chartered Banks and Thrifts May Provide Custody Services for Crypto Assets
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

title: MicroStrategy adopts Bitcoin as a treasury reserve asset
summary: MicroStrategy announced a $250 million purchase of 21,454 BTC as part of a new capital-allocation strategy.
details: The publicly traded software company described bitcoin as its primary treasury reserve asset alongside cash. It later used debt and equity issuance to acquire substantially more.
whyItMatters: The purchase established a highly visible corporate-treasury model that other public companies later examined or copied.

title: lnd adds support for larger Wumbo channels
summary: Lightning Labs released lnd 0.11-beta with optional support for channels above the network's early safety limit.
details: The previous 0.1677 BTC channel cap had constrained large routing nodes while the technology matured. Wumbo channels required both peers to opt in and did not alter Bitcoin base-layer consensus.
whyItMatters: Larger channels increased Lightning's capacity for professional routing and higher-value payments.

sources.title: Announcing lnd 0.11-beta: Let's Get Ready to Wumbo

technicalNote: Wumbo is a negotiated Lightning feature bit that permits channels larger than 0.1677 BTC.

title: Wyoming approves Kraken's special-purpose bank charter
summary: Kraken received approval to form a Wyoming special-purpose depository institution focused on digital assets.
details: Kraken Financial was designed to offer custody and related banking services under state supervision. The charter was not the same as FDIC insurance and did not make exchange deposits federally insured.
whyItMatters: The approval created a new bridge between a major cryptocurrency exchange and U.S. banking law.

title: U.S. authorities charge BitMEX founders
summary: Federal prosecutors charged BitMEX founders with Bank Secrecy Act violations while the CFTC filed a parallel civil action.
details: The criminal case alleged willful failure to establish and maintain an adequate anti-money-laundering program. The exchange remained operational and later changed leadership and compliance practices.
whyItMatters: The action showed that offshore Bitcoin derivatives venues serving U.S. customers faced direct U.S. enforcement risk.

sources.title: Founders And Executives Of Off-Shore Cryptocurrency Derivatives Exchange Charged With Violation Of The Bank Secrecy Act

title: Square invests $50 million in Bitcoin
summary: Payments company Square announced that it had purchased approximately 4,709 BTC for its corporate balance sheet.
details: The company said the purchase represented about one percent of its assets at the end of the prior quarter. It also published an open-source investment memo describing execution and custody practices.
whyItMatters: A major payments company paired corporate adoption with a reusable operational playbook.

title: PayPal announces cryptocurrency buying and merchant use
summary: PayPal said U.S. customers would be able to buy, hold, and sell bitcoin and use supported crypto balances at checkout.
details: Checkout payments were converted to fiat for merchants, so merchants did not directly receive bitcoin. The initial product was custodial and did not allow external wallet transfers.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin exposure entered a mainstream payments account used by hundreds of millions of customers.

sources.title: PayPal Launches New Service Enabling Users to Buy, Hold and Sell Cryptocurrency

title: U.S. announces seizure of over 69,000 BTC linked to Silk Road
summary: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint after taking control of bitcoin allegedly connected to the Silk Road marketplace.
details: The assets had been held for years by an individual identified in the complaint as Individual X. The case later became part of the federal government's large forfeited-bitcoin holdings.
whyItMatters: The seizure showed how old on-chain proceeds could become recoverable state assets years after their movement.

sources.title: United States Files a Civil Action to Forfeit Cryptocurrency Valued at Over One Billion U.S. Dollars

title: MassMutual adds Bitcoin to its general investment account
summary: Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance disclosed a $100 million Bitcoin purchase and an equity investment in custody provider NYDIG.
details: The allocation was small relative to the insurer's general investment account and was framed as part of a broader diversification strategy. NYDIG provided custody for the bitcoin.
whyItMatters: A long-established life insurer became an early regulated institutional holder of Bitcoin.

title: Bitcoin moves above its 2017 market record
summary: Major price indexes recorded Bitcoin decisively above the peak reached during the 2017 cycle.
details: The move followed growing corporate treasury purchases, institutional products, and an unusually expansionary global monetary environment. Prices vary across venues, so the exact record level depends on the selected index.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin completed its first recovery beyond a prior cycle's widely watched peak.

title: OCC permits banks to use blockchain networks for payments
summary: The OCC said U.S. national banks may participate in independent node verification networks and use stablecoins for permissible payment activities.
details: Interpretive Letter 1174 addressed bank-operated nodes and payment functions rather than authorizing every cryptocurrency activity. It extended the agency's earlier custody analysis into distributed payment infrastructure.
whyItMatters: The letter placed some public-blockchain payment operations within the recognized business of federally chartered banks.
actors: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: Federally Chartered Banks and Thrifts May Participate in Independent Node Verification Networks
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

title: Nigeria orders banks to close crypto accounts
summary: The central bank directed financial institutions to identify and close accounts tied to cryptocurrency exchanges.
details: Nigeria was among the largest peer-to-peer bitcoin markets in the world, driven by currency controls and remittance costs. Trading moved to peer-to-peer channels rather than stopping, and the restriction was lifted in December 2023.
whyItMatters: It is the clearest natural experiment in whether cutting banking access removes demand or merely moves it underground.

sources.title: Letter to banks on dealings in cryptocurrencies

title: Tesla discloses a $1.5 billion Bitcoin purchase
summary: Tesla's annual filing disclosed that the company had invested $1.5 billion in bitcoin under a revised treasury policy.
details: The filing also said Tesla expected to begin accepting bitcoin for products on a limited basis. Tesla briefly enabled that option before suspending it later in the year.
whyItMatters: One of the world's most closely watched public companies moved Bitcoin treasury adoption into mainstream corporate debate.

title: BNY Mellon creates a digital-assets unit
summary: BNY Mellon announced a unit to develop custody and administration for digital assets alongside traditional holdings.
details: The bank described plans for an integrated multi-asset platform serving investment clients. Its actual service rollout depended on technology, client demand, and regulatory approvals.
whyItMatters: The world's largest custodian bank publicly committed to supporting institutional digital-asset infrastructure.

title: Purpose Bitcoin ETF begins trading in Canada
summary: Purpose Investments launched a physically backed Bitcoin ETF on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
details: The fund held bitcoin in institutional cold storage and offered Canadian-dollar and U.S.-dollar units. It was the first directly settled Bitcoin ETF available to retail investors in North America.
whyItMatters: Canada demonstrated a regulated spot Bitcoin fund structure years before U.S. spot products were approved.

title: Coinbase lists publicly on Nasdaq
summary: Coinbase shares began trading through a direct listing on Nasdaq under the ticker COIN.
details: The listing gave public-market investors direct equity exposure to a large U.S. cryptocurrency exchange. It also subjected Coinbase to ongoing public-company reporting and governance requirements.
whyItMatters: A Bitcoin-native exchange entered major U.S. equity markets without a traditional initial public offering.

title: Turkey prohibits crypto assets in payments
summary: Turkey's central bank issued a regulation barring crypto assets from direct or indirect use in payments.
details: The rule did not prohibit owning or trading bitcoin, but it blocked payment-service providers from building payment flows around crypto assets. It took effect on April 30.
whyItMatters: The measure distinguished legal trading from prohibited payment use in a large inflation-sensitive market.
actors: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

sources.title: Regulation on the Disuse of Crypto Assets in Payments
sources.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

title: Tesla suspends vehicle purchases with Bitcoin
summary: Tesla stopped accepting bitcoin for vehicle purchases, citing concerns about fossil-fuel use in mining and transactions.
details: The company said it would retain rather than immediately sell the bitcoin it held and would reconsider payments if mining used more sustainable energy. The announcement prompted renewed debate over measurement of Bitcoin's environmental footprint.
whyItMatters: A high-profile reversal showed how mining-energy concerns could constrain merchant adoption even after a major launch.

title: China's State Council committee calls for a Bitcoin mining crackdown
summary: A State Council financial committee called for cracking down on Bitcoin mining and trading activities.
details: Provincial authorities subsequently ordered or encouraged mining facilities to close, and access to power and financing tightened. China had previously hosted a large share of global hash rate.
whyItMatters: The policy triggered the fastest geographic redistribution of Bitcoin mining in the network's history.

sources.title: China to Crack Down on Bitcoin Mining and Trading

title: El Salvador's president announces a Bitcoin legal-tender bill
summary: President Nayib Bukele announced that he would send legislation making Bitcoin legal tender to El Salvador's assembly.
details: The announcement was delivered by video at a Bitcoin conference in Miami. A short bill followed within days and moved rapidly through the legislature.
whyItMatters: A national government publicly committed for the first time to giving Bitcoin legal-tender status.

sources.title: El Salvador Plans to Make Bitcoin Legal Tender

title: The FBI recovers a ransomware payment in bitcoin
summary: U.S. authorities seized about 63.7 BTC of the ransom Colonial Pipeline had paid to the DarkSide group.
details: Investigators traced the payment across the public ledger and obtained the private key for the receiving wallet. The pipeline shutdown had caused fuel shortages across the U.S. east coast weeks earlier.
whyItMatters: It publicly contradicted the assumption that bitcoin payments are untraceable, using nothing but the ledger and ordinary police work.

sources.title: Department of Justice Seizes $2.3 Million in Cryptocurrency Paid to the Ransomware Extortionists Darkside

title: El Salvador passes the Bitcoin Law
summary: El Salvador's Legislative Assembly approved a law giving Bitcoin legal-tender status alongside the U.S. dollar.
details: The original text required economic agents to accept bitcoin when offered, subject to limited exceptions, and required the state to facilitate convertibility. It set a 90-day period before taking effect.
whyItMatters: El Salvador became the first sovereign state to enact Bitcoin legal-tender legislation.

title: Taproot locks in through Speedy Trial
summary: Miner signaling met the Speedy Trial threshold, locking Taproot in for activation at block 709632.
details: The deployment bundled Schnorr signatures, Taproot output rules, and Tapscript. Lock-in meant upgraded nodes would begin enforcing the new rules at the scheduled November height.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin's first major consensus upgrade since SegWit secured broad activation without a contentious chain split.
technicalNote: Speedy Trial used BIP9 signaling with mandatory activation enforcement at height 709632.

title: Sichuan orders major Bitcoin mining operations to close
summary: Authorities in Sichuan directed power companies to inspect and cut supply to identified cryptocurrency mining projects.
details: Sichuan's seasonal hydropower had made it an important mining center. The shutdown followed similar restrictions in other Chinese regions and contributed to a steep short-term hash-rate decline.
whyItMatters: The order dismantled one of Bitcoin mining's largest geographic concentrations within days.
actors: Sichuan Provincial Development and Reform Commission

sources.title: China's Cryptocurrency-Mining Crackdown Spreads to Sichuan

title: Difficulty falls by a record 28%
summary: Bitcoin's largest ever downward difficulty adjustment followed China's removal of roughly half the network's hash rate.
details: Provincial shutdowns had switched off a large share of global mining within weeks, leaving blocks arriving far slower than the ten-minute target. The retarget restored normal block times automatically, and hash rate returned within a year from North America and Central Asia.
whyItMatters: It is the strongest demonstration that Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment absorbs the loss of half its miners without any intervention.
technicalNote: The adjustment was approximately −27.94% at block 689,472, the largest downward retarget in Bitcoin's history.

title: El Salvador's Bitcoin Law takes effect
summary: Bitcoin's legal-tender status began in El Salvador as the government launched the Chivo wallet and related infrastructure.
details: The rollout included a state-backed conversion trust, ATMs, and a $30 equivalent incentive for eligible wallet users. Launch-day technical problems and public protests accompanied the policy's implementation.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin moved from a private monetary network into a live national legal-tender experiment.

sources.title: El Salvador's Bitcoin Law Comes into Force

title: China declares virtual-currency business activities illegal
summary: Chinese authorities issued a coordinated notice treating a broad range of virtual-currency trading services as illegal financial activity.
details: The notice covered exchange, matching, derivatives, and services provided by offshore platforms to mainland residents. Holding bitcoin itself was not described in the same way as operating prohibited financial business.
whyItMatters: The measure consolidated China's trading restrictions into its broadest national prohibition to date.

sources.title: Notice on Further Preventing and Disposing of Risks in Virtual Currency Trading

title: The first U.S. bitcoin ETF begins trading
summary: ProShares listed a fund holding bitcoin futures rather than bitcoin itself.
details: The SEC had allowed a futures-based product under the Investment Company Act while continuing to reject spot funds. Rolling futures contracts imposed a cost that made the fund track bitcoin imperfectly over time.
whyItMatters: It gave U.S. brokerage accounts their first bitcoin exposure, and made the SEC's continued refusal of spot funds harder to defend.

title: Bitcoin reaches its 2021 cycle high
summary: Bitcoin traded near $69,000 on major dollar markets before beginning a prolonged decline.
details: Exact intraday highs differ by exchange and benchmark, so the level is conventionally rounded. The market peak arrived amid elevated inflation readings, leverage, and broad digital-asset speculation.
whyItMatters: The high became the reference point for the 2022 market contraction and subsequent recovery.

title: Taproot activates on Bitcoin
summary: Taproot activated at block 709632, adding Schnorr signatures, new spending rules, and more flexible scripts.
details: Taproot lets simple key-path spends look alike on-chain while preserving optional complex script paths. Tapscript removed several old limits and made future script extensions easier.
whyItMatters: The upgrade improved privacy and efficiency for many advanced spending policies and expanded Bitcoin's programmable foundation.
technicalNote: Activation enforced BIP 341 and BIP 342 rules from block 709632 onward.

title: U.S. infrastructure law expands digital-asset reporting provisions
summary: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act added digital-asset broker reporting language to the U.S. tax code.
details: The broad statutory wording prompted debate about whether miners, developers, and wallet providers could fall within the broker definition. Later Treasury rulemaking narrowed practical reporting obligations and implementation dates.
whyItMatters: Digital-asset tax reporting moved from agency guidance into major federal legislation.

sources.title: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Public Law 117-58

title: Canada freezes protest-linked accounts under emergency powers
summary: Invoking the Emergencies Act, the government directed banks to freeze accounts tied to the trucker convoy, and named crypto addresses.
details: The order required financial institutions to stop servicing designated persons without a court order, and an RCMP list circulated to exchanges included bitcoin addresses. A federal court later found the invocation unreasonable and unconstitutional.
whyItMatters: A wealthy democracy froze accounts by executive order, which moved censorship resistance from a theoretical property to an argument about a specific week.

title: Ukraine publishes addresses for cryptocurrency donations
summary: Ukraine's government shared bitcoin and other cryptocurrency addresses for donations after Russia's full-scale invasion.
details: Donors sent funds directly on public networks, while aid groups also received substantial crypto contributions. The event did not replace conventional aid but demonstrated fast cross-border fundraising under wartime constraints.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin became part of a sovereign government's emergency donation infrastructure during an active war.

title: United States issues a government-wide digital-assets order
summary: President Joe Biden signed an executive order directing coordinated federal work on digital-asset risks and opportunities.
details: The order covered consumer protection, financial stability, illicit finance, U.S. competitiveness, inclusion, and technology. It initiated reports and policy frameworks rather than creating a Bitcoin-specific regulatory regime by itself.
whyItMatters: Digital assets became a formal cross-agency policy priority for the U.S. executive branch.

sources.title: Executive Order on Ensuring Responsible Development of Digital Assets

title: Lightning Labs proposes Taro for Taproot-based assets
summary: Lightning Labs announced Taro, later renamed Taproot Assets, for issuing assets anchored in Bitcoin transactions.
details: The proposal used Taproot commitments and off-chain proofs so asset metadata did not have to occupy ordinary Bitcoin transaction fields. Its longer-term design included routing asset payments over Lightning with bitcoin as an intermediary.
whyItMatters: Taproot's new commitment structure began supporting an ecosystem of asset protocols beyond native bitcoin transfers.

sources.title: Announcing Taro: A New Protocol for Multi-Asset Bitcoin and Lightning

technicalNote: The protocol commits asset state into Taproot outputs while proofs are transferred separately from the base chain.

title: Fidelity announces Bitcoin access for workplace retirement plans
summary: Fidelity introduced a workplace Digital Assets Account that eligible employers could add to 401(k) plan menus.
details: The account combined bitcoin exposure with short-term money-market holdings and imposed plan-level limits. Employers retained fiduciary responsibility for deciding whether to offer it.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin exposure entered the architecture of U.S. employer-sponsored retirement savings.

sources.title: Fidelity to Offer First-of-Its-Kind Bitcoin Option for 401(k) Plans

title: Central African Republic adopts Bitcoin as legal tender
summary: The Central African Republic announced legislation making Bitcoin legal tender alongside the CFA franc.
details: The measure was adopted with limited public implementation detail and drew concerns from regional monetary authorities and the IMF. The country later reversed the legal-tender provision in 2023.
whyItMatters: The Central African Republic became the second country to enact national Bitcoin legal-tender status.
actors: Government of the Central African Republic

sources.title: IMF Staff Completes Mission to the Central African Republic

title: Terra's stablecoin system enters a collapse
summary: TerraUSD lost its intended dollar peg and the associated LUNA token entered a hyperinflationary collapse.
details: The failure was not a Bitcoin protocol event, although reserves associated with the project had included a large bitcoin position. Losses and forced deleveraging spread through lenders, funds, and trading firms across the wider market.
whyItMatters: Terra's failure became the first shock in a chain of 2022 insolvencies that reshaped Bitcoin credit markets.

title: Celsius pauses withdrawals and transfers
summary: Crypto lender Celsius froze customer withdrawals, swaps, and transfers, citing extreme market conditions.
details: The pause trapped customer assets and revealed severe liquidity and asset-liability mismatches. Celsius filed for Chapter 11 protection the following month.
whyItMatters: The freeze exposed the bank-like risks of centralized Bitcoin yield products without equivalent depositor protections.

sources.title: A Memo to the Celsius Community

title: Three Arrows Capital is ordered into liquidation
summary: A British Virgin Islands court ordered the liquidation of cryptocurrency hedge fund Three Arrows Capital.
details: The fund had taken large leveraged positions and suffered losses linked to Terra and falling crypto markets. Its default transmitted losses to brokers and lenders that had extended under-collateralized credit.
whyItMatters: The failure revealed dense and poorly disclosed counterparty links across centralized Bitcoin credit markets.

sources.title: Three Arrows Capital Ordered Into Liquidation

title: EU institutions reach political agreement on MiCA
summary: European negotiators reached a provisional agreement on the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation.
details: The framework covered crypto-asset issuers and service providers not already governed by other EU financial law. Bitcoin itself has no issuer, but exchanges, custodians, and market conduct around it fall within important parts of the regime.
whyItMatters: The agreement set the path for the first comprehensive, passportable crypto-service framework across the European Union.

sources.title: Digital Finance: Agreement Reached on European Crypto-Assets Regulation

title: Voyager Digital files for bankruptcy
summary: The crypto lender collapsed after a large loan to Three Arrows Capital went unpaid.
details: Customers had been told their deposits were protected, language the FDIC later said was misleading because the insurance covered the bank holding Voyager's own funds, not customer crypto. Retail depositors were left as unsecured creditors.
whyItMatters: It exposed how far consumer-facing yield products had drifted from the deposit insurance customers believed they had.

sources.title: FDIC demands Voyager Digital cease making false representations

title: Tesla discloses sale of most of its Bitcoin position
summary: Tesla reported converting about 75 percent of its bitcoin holdings into fiat currency during the second quarter.
details: The company said the sale added $936 million of cash and described liquidity during COVID-related uncertainty as a factor. Tesla retained a smaller position rather than fully exiting Bitcoin.
whyItMatters: The sale demonstrated that prominent corporate-treasury adoption could be reversible under balance-sheet pressure.

sources.title: Tesla Quarterly Report for the Quarter Ended June 30, 2022

title: OFAC sanctions a privacy tool rather than a person
summary: The U.S. Treasury added the Tornado Cash mixing contracts to its sanctions list.
details: The designation targeted autonomous software rather than an identifiable operator, making it unlawful for U.S. persons to interact with the code. A court later held that immutable smart contracts were not property that could be designated, and the listing was removed in 2025.
whyItMatters: It opened the question of whether publishing privacy software is itself sanctionable conduct, which bears directly on Bitcoin tooling.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Notorious Virtual Currency Mixer Tornado Cash

title: Norwegian court rules for hodlonaut in Craig Wright case
summary: Oslo District Court found that public statements calling Craig Wright's Satoshi claim fraudulent were protected in context.
details: The dispute arose after Wright asserted that he was Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto and threatened defamation claims. The Norwegian ruling was jurisdiction-specific and preceded a broader U.K. identity trial.
whyItMatters: The decision reduced legal pressure on a prominent critic and foreshadowed later judicial rejection of Wright's authorship claims.

sources.title: Hodlonaut Wins Norwegian Lawsuit Against Craig Wright

title: FTX files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: FTX Trading and more than one hundred affiliates entered U.S. bankruptcy proceedings after a rapid liquidity crisis.
details: The collapse followed revelations about the relationship between FTX and Alameda Research and a wave of customer withdrawals. Later criminal proceedings established fraud by senior executives, but the November filing itself was the start of the restructuring process.
whyItMatters: The failure of a leading exchange caused major customer losses, market contagion, and a global reassessment of custody and proof-of-reserves claims.

sources.title: FTX Trading Ltd. Chapter 11 case docket
SEC Charges Samuel Bankman-Fried with Defrauding Investors in Crypto Asset Trading Platform FTX

title: Bitcoin bottoms near $15,500 after FTX
summary: The price reached its cycle low ten days after FTX filed for bankruptcy.
details: The year had removed Terra, Celsius, Three Arrows, Voyager, BlockFi and FTX from the market in sequence. The protocol itself produced blocks throughout without interruption.
whyItMatters: The low point of the worst year for crypto institutions was not caused by, and did not affect, anything in Bitcoin's consensus rules.

title: New York enacts a targeted proof-of-work mining moratorium
summary: New York imposed a two-year pause on certain new or expanded fossil-fuel power permits for proof-of-work mining.
details: The law did not ban all Bitcoin mining and did not apply retroactively to every existing facility. It paired the permit pause with a state environmental-impact study.
whyItMatters: New York became the first U.S. state to enact a mining restriction explicitly tied to proof-of-work energy use.
actors: New York Department of Environmental Conservation

sources.title: Ruling on the Cryptocurrency Mining Moratorium
sources.publisher: New York Department of Environmental Conservation

title: BlockFi files for bankruptcy
summary: Crypto lender BlockFi and several affiliates filed for Chapter 11 protection after suspending withdrawals.
details: BlockFi had significant exposure to FTX and Alameda Research after earlier losses in the 2022 credit crisis. The filing listed a large customer and institutional creditor base.
whyItMatters: The bankruptcy extended FTX contagion into a major retail Bitcoin lending platform.

title: Basel Committee publishes its bank crypto-asset standard
summary: The Basel Committee finalized a prudential treatment for banks' crypto-asset exposures, including a conservative category for Bitcoin.
details: Unbacked crypto assets such as bitcoin fall into a higher-risk group with stringent capital treatment and an aggregate exposure limit. The standard set an international baseline subject to implementation by member jurisdictions.
whyItMatters: Global bank supervisors established common capital constraints for direct Bitcoin exposure.

title: Core Scientific files for Chapter 11
summary: Large publicly traded Bitcoin miner Core Scientific entered bankruptcy protection after falling prices and rising power costs strained its finances.
details: The company continued mining while restructuring rather than liquidating immediately. Its difficulties also reflected debt, equipment commitments, and exposure to failed customer Celsius.
whyItMatters: The filing showed how industrial miners could remain operationally productive while becoming financially insolvent.

title: El Salvador approves a digital-asset issuance law
summary: El Salvador's assembly approved a framework for public offerings of digital assets and sovereign digital-asset securities.
details: The law created a digital-assets commission and an issuance agency separate from the country's original Bitcoin Law. It was designed in part to support proposed Bitcoin-linked sovereign financing, although passage did not itself complete any bond issuance.
whyItMatters: El Salvador extended its Bitcoin policy from payments into capital-markets infrastructure.

title: Genesis files for bankruptcy
summary: The lending arm of Digital Currency Group entered Chapter 11, freezing funds owed to retail lenders.
details: Genesis had halted withdrawals in November after FTX collapsed, stranding the assets behind Gemini's Earn product. The SEC charged both firms with offering unregistered securities through it.
whyItMatters: It carried FTX's failure into the group that also owned Grayscale, the vehicle holding the largest pool of institutional bitcoin.

sources.title: SEC Charges Genesis and Gemini for the Unregistered Offer and Sale of Crypto Asset Securities

title: Ordinals brings inscriptions to Bitcoin
summary: Casey Rodarmor released the Ordinals protocol and tooling for tracking individual satoshis and attaching inscriptions to them.
details: Inscriptions place content in Taproot witness data and identify the resulting satoshi through an off-chain numbering convention. The protocol required no Bitcoin consensus change, but it produced new demand for block space and renewed debate over transaction policy.
whyItMatters: Ordinals opened a major new use of Bitcoin block space for digital artifacts and later fungible-token experiments.
technicalNote: Ordinal theory is an index and convention layered on ordinary valid Bitcoin transactions; nodes do not enforce ordinal ownership as consensus.

title: Silvergate announces a voluntary wind-down
summary: Silvergate Capital said it would wind down Silvergate Bank and voluntarily liquidate it under regulatory supervision.
details: The crypto-focused bank had suffered heavy deposit outflows and losses after the FTX collapse. Its SEN payments network had provided always-on dollar settlement for many exchanges and trading firms.
whyItMatters: The closure removed a central banking and settlement connection from the institutional Bitcoin market.

sources.title: Silvergate Capital Announces Intent to Wind Down Operations and Voluntarily Liquidate Silvergate Bank

title: The BRC-20 token experiment begins
summary: A pseudonymous developer deployed an experimental convention for fungible tokens using JSON inscriptions on Bitcoin.
details: BRC-20 state is interpreted by external indexers rather than by Bitcoin's consensus rules. Activity grew rapidly and contributed to higher fees, but implementations had to coordinate closely to avoid inconsistent balances.
whyItMatters: The experiment expanded Ordinals from unique artifacts into high-volume token activity on Bitcoin block space.
technicalNote: BRC-20 is an off-chain indexing convention, not a BIP or a Bitcoin consensus feature.

title: New York regulators close Signature Bank
summary: New York's banking regulator took possession of Signature Bank and the FDIC was appointed receiver.
details: Signature had served cryptocurrency firms through its Signet real-time payments network, although it had a broader commercial banking business. Authorities invoked systemic-risk measures to protect all depositors while equity and certain debt holders were not protected.
whyItMatters: The closure further reduced U.S. dollar banking access for Bitcoin exchanges days after Silvergate's wind-down.
actors: New York Department of Financial Services

title: Central African Republic removes Bitcoin's legal-tender status
summary: A revised cryptocurrency law removed legal-tender status and guaranteed convertibility for crypto assets in the Central African Republic.
details: The amendment aligned national law more closely with the CEMAC monetary union and its CFA franc framework. Cryptocurrency transactions remained possible under a narrower and still-developing legal framework.
whyItMatters: The world's second national Bitcoin legal-tender experiment was formally reversed after less than one year.
actors: Government of the Central African Republic
technicalNote: The National Assembly repealed the legal-tender provision on 23 March 2023. The IMF country report documenting the change was published later that year.

title: Council of the EU formally adopts MiCA
summary: The Council completed the legislative adoption of the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation.
details: MiCA established harmonized rules for crypto-asset service providers, market conduct, and several token categories across the EU. Bitcoin has no issuer, so issuer-specific requirements do not map to it in the same way as to centrally issued assets.
whyItMatters: A comprehensive regional crypto framework moved from negotiation into binding European law.

sources.title: Digital Finance: Council Adopts New Rules on Markets in Crypto-Assets

title: Bitcoin passes ten million Ordinals inscriptions
summary: Public Ordinals indexes counted the ten-millionth inscription roughly four months after the protocol's release.
details: Most inscriptions were small text or token-related records rather than large images. The milestone arrived during elevated fee competition and showed that inscription demand had become a durable block-space factor.
whyItMatters: Ordinals moved from a niche experiment to a material source of Bitcoin transactions and miner fee revenue.

title: Hong Kong's virtual-asset platform licensing regime begins
summary: Hong Kong brought centralized virtual-asset trading platforms under a new Securities and Futures Commission licensing system.
details: The regime included custody, governance, token due-diligence, and investor-protection requirements. Licensed platforms could serve retail clients subject to suitability and token-admission safeguards.
whyItMatters: Hong Kong reopened a regulated path for retail Bitcoin trading as mainland China maintained broad restrictions.
actors: Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission

sources.title: SFC Concludes Consultation on Regulation of Virtual Asset Trading Platforms
sources.publisher: Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission

title: The SEC sues Binance and Coinbase in consecutive days
summary: The agency filed suit against the largest offshore exchange and the largest U.S. one within twenty-four hours.
details: Both complaints alleged operating unregistered exchanges; neither treated bitcoin itself as a security, a distinction the agency had held to consistently. The Coinbase case was dismissed in 2025 after a change in the agency's approach.
whyItMatters: Regulation by enforcement reached its high-water mark here, and the resulting backlash drove the push for market-structure legislation.
technicalNote: Neither complaint alleged that bitcoin is a security. The agency has treated bitcoin as a non-security since 2018.

sources.title: SEC Files 13 Charges Against Binance Entities and Founder Changpeng Zhao
SEC Charges Coinbase for Operating as an Unregistered Securities Exchange

title: BlackRock files for a U.S. spot Bitcoin product
summary: Nasdaq filed to list BlackRock's proposed iShares Bitcoin Trust as a commodity-based trust holding bitcoin.
details: The filing proposed Coinbase Custody as custodian and later added a surveillance-sharing arrangement tied to spot trading. Competing issuers quickly updated or renewed their own applications.
whyItMatters: The world's largest asset manager transformed the long-running spot ETF contest into an institutional race that ended in approval.

sources.title: Notice of Filing to List and Trade Shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust

title: Brazil's virtual-assets legal framework takes effect
summary: Brazil's law governing virtual-asset service providers entered into force with the central bank designated as the principal regulator.
details: The framework addressed authorization, governance, consumer protection, and financial-crime controls for intermediaries. It did not make bitcoin legal tender or guarantee cryptocurrency investments.
whyItMatters: Latin America's largest economy established a national licensing foundation for Bitcoin service providers.

title: United Kingdom brings crypto assets into financial-services law
summary: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 received Royal Assent with powers to regulate crypto-asset activities and promotions.
details: The act created enabling authority rather than a complete Bitcoin rulebook on the day it passed. Detailed requirements continued through Treasury, FCA, and secondary-legislation processes.
whyItMatters: The U.K. established a statutory basis for moving Bitcoin services into its mainstream financial regulatory perimeter.

title: Grayscale wins its appeal against the SEC
summary: The D.C. Circuit vacated the SEC's denial of Grayscale's proposal to convert GBTC into a spot Bitcoin ETP.
details: The court held that the agency failed to explain its different treatment of similar spot and futures-based products. The ruling returned the matter to the SEC and did not itself approve the conversion.
whyItMatters: The judgment removed the central legal obstacle to U.S. spot Bitcoin ETP approvals.
actors: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

sources.title: Grayscale v. SEC Opinion
sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

title: BitVM proposes verifiable computation on Bitcoin
summary: Robin Linus published a white paper describing how complex computations could be challenged through Bitcoin transactions without a consensus change.
details: The original design used large pre-signed transaction graphs and an optimistic dispute model between parties. It was a research proposal, not a production virtual machine running directly in Bitcoin consensus.
whyItMatters: BitVM renewed technical exploration of trust-minimized bridges and advanced contracts anchored to Bitcoin.
technicalNote: BitVM uses Bitcoin Script for fraud proofs and off-chain computation rather than adding general computation to base-layer consensus.

title: Binance and its founder enter U.S. guilty pleas
summary: Binance agreed to more than $4 billion in U.S. resolutions and founder Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to an anti-money-laundering charge.
details: The company admitted Bank Secrecy Act, unlicensed money-transmitting, and sanctions violations. Zhao resigned as chief executive, and the settlement imposed compliance monitoring and other obligations.
whyItMatters: The largest global crypto exchange accepted one of the largest corporate criminal resolutions in U.S. history.

sources.title: Binance and CEO Plead Guilty to Federal Charges in $4B Resolution

title: FASB adopts fair-value accounting for covered crypto assets
summary: The Financial Accounting Standards Board required qualifying crypto assets such as bitcoin to be measured at fair value each reporting period.
details: Changes in fair value would be recognized in net income, replacing the prior indefinite-lived intangible impairment model for covered holdings. The standard applied to fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024, with early adoption permitted.
whyItMatters: U.S. corporate Bitcoin accounting began reflecting both gains and losses instead of recognizing only impairment until sale.

sources.title: FASB Issues Standard to Improve Accounting for Crypto Assets

title: Nigeria reopens banking to crypto firms
summary: The central bank replaced its 2021 prohibition with a licensing and account-opening framework.
details: The new guidance acknowledged that the restriction had pushed activity into peer-to-peer channels outside any supervision. Banks were permitted to serve licensed virtual-asset service providers under defined conditions.
whyItMatters: A major regulator reversed a ban on the explicit ground that it had made oversight harder rather than easier.

sources.title: Guidelines on operations of bank accounts for virtual asset service providers

title: SEC social account is compromised before the ETF decision
summary: An attacker used a SIM swap to access the SEC's X account and post a false notice that spot Bitcoin products had been approved.
details: The agency removed the post and said no approval had occurred at that time. The real Commission decision followed the next day, while law enforcement continued investigating the intrusion.
whyItMatters: The incident briefly moved Bitcoin markets and highlighted security risks around authoritative regulatory communications.

title: SEC approves U.S. spot Bitcoin ETP listings
summary: The SEC approved exchange rule changes allowing multiple spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products to list in the United States.
details: The omnibus decision followed the Grayscale court ruling and covered products from established and crypto-focused asset managers. Approval applied to the product structures and did not constitute an endorsement of Bitcoin.
whyItMatters: U.S. investors gained brokerage-account access to funds that directly hold bitcoin after a decade of rejected applications.

sources.title: Statement on the Approval of Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Products

title: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs begin trading
summary: New spot Bitcoin products began trading on Nasdaq, NYSE Arca, and Cboe alongside Grayscale's converted trust.
details: The group generated about $4.6 billion in first-day trading volume, with substantial flows and transfers between products. Authorized participants created and redeemed shares while custodians held the underlying bitcoin.
whyItMatters: A large new regulated distribution channel connected Bitcoin spot holdings to U.S. brokerage and advisory markets.

sources.title: SEC approves spot bitcoin exchange-traded product listings

title: U.K. judge rules that Craig Wright is not Satoshi
summary: At the close of trial, the High Court declared that Craig Wright did not create Bitcoin, write its white paper, or use the Satoshi Nakamoto identity.
details: A detailed May judgment explained the evidentiary findings, including extensive document fabrication. The court later issued injunctions and referred materials to prosecutors, while appeals and related orders followed separate procedures.
whyItMatters: A comprehensive judicial record rejected the most persistent public claim to Satoshi's identity and protected developers from related copyright assertions.
actors: High Court of England and Wales

title: Bitcoin's fourth halving reduces the subsidy to 3.125 BTC
summary: Block 840000 cut the block subsidy from 6.25 BTC to 3.125 BTC.
details: The programmed change reduced expected new issuance to roughly 450 BTC per day at ten-minute blocks. Unusually high transaction fees around the same block temporarily exceeded the subsidy because of Runes activity.
whyItMatters: The fourth halving advanced Bitcoin into an epoch where fee revenue plays a larger role in miner economics.
technicalNote: The consensus subsidy became 3.125 BTC at the fourth 210,000-block boundary.

title: Runes launches at the fourth halving
summary: Casey Rodarmor's Runes protocol began at block 840000 as a fungible-token convention based on Bitcoin UTXOs.
details: Runes encodes protocol messages in OP_RETURN outputs and relies on an external indexing convention. Launch demand contributed to a surge in transaction fees, but Runes did not change Bitcoin consensus.
whyItMatters: A second major token system expanded competition for Bitcoin block space at a symbolically important block.
technicalNote: Runes is a UTXO-indexing protocol whose messages are carried in standard Bitcoin transactions.

title: Samourai Wallet's founders are arrested
summary: U.S. prosecutors charged the developers of a bitcoin privacy wallet with money laundering and unlicensed money transmission.
details: The service was non-custodial: it coordinated transactions between users without ever holding their coins. Prosecutors argued the coordination itself constituted money transmission, a reading that would reach much self-custody software.
whyItMatters: It put the question directly: whether writing bitcoin privacy software is a crime when other people use it badly.

sources.title: Founders And CEO Of Cryptocurrency Mixing Service Arrested And Charged With Money Laundering And Unlicensed Money Transmitting Offenses

title: Hong Kong spot Bitcoin ETFs begin trading
summary: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing listed the region's first spot virtual-asset ETFs, including three Bitcoin funds.
details: The products offered cash and, for eligible participants, in-kind subscription or redemption arrangements. Their market scale was smaller than the U.S. launch but added a regulated Asian spot channel.
whyItMatters: Hong Kong became a leading Asian jurisdiction for exchange-listed funds that directly hold bitcoin.
actors: Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission

sources.title: HKEX Welcomes Asia's First Spot Virtual Asset ETFs

title: Wisconsin investment board discloses Bitcoin ETF holdings
summary: The State of Wisconsin Investment Board reported positions in spot Bitcoin funds in its quarterly U.S. securities filing.
details: The disclosure included shares of BlackRock's IBIT and Grayscale's GBTC as of March 31. A Form 13F reports listed-security holdings and does not by itself reveal the full investment rationale or all portfolio exposure.
whyItMatters: A U.S. public pension manager became an early disclosed institutional holder of spot Bitcoin ETP shares.

sources.title: State of Wisconsin Investment Board Form 13F

title: FIT21 digital-asset bill passes the U.S. House
summary: The House approved the Financial Innovation and Technology for the 21st Century Act by a bipartisan 279-136 vote.
details: The bill proposed a market-structure division of responsibilities between the SEC and CFTC. It did not become law in that Congress, so its passage marked legislative direction rather than a binding regulatory change.
whyItMatters: A comprehensive digital-asset market-structure proposal cleared one chamber of Congress for the first time.

sources.title: Congressional Record: Financial Innovation and Technology for the 21st Century Act

title: DMM Bitcoin loses 4,502 BTC
summary: The Japanese exchange disclosed an unauthorised outflow worth roughly $305 million, the largest bitcoin theft of the year.
details: The company covered customer balances with group funding and wound down the following year, transferring accounts to another operator. Investigators attributed the theft to North Korean actors.
whyItMatters: A decade after Mt. Gox, a regulated Japanese exchange still lost thousands of bitcoin from its own systems.

sources.title: Japan's DMM Bitcoin says $482 million worth of bitcoin leaked

title: President Biden vetoes repeal of SEC custody accounting guidance
summary: President Joe Biden vetoed a congressional resolution that would have overturned SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin 121.
details: SAB 121 directed certain public companies safeguarding customer crypto assets to recognize corresponding assets and liabilities on their balance sheets. Congress could not override the veto, and the guidance remained until SEC staff rescinded it in January 2025.
whyItMatters: The veto preserved a contested accounting treatment that affected banks considering Bitcoin custody.

sources.title: H.J.Res.109 - Providing for Congressional Disapproval of SAB 121

title: Mt. Gox begins Bitcoin repayments
summary: The Mt. Gox rehabilitation trustee made the first bitcoin and bitcoin cash repayments through designated exchanges.
details: Eligible creditors had waited about a decade after the exchange's collapse. Distribution timing varied by exchange, identity checks, account status, and completion of required agreements.
whyItMatters: One of Bitcoin's longest insolvency proceedings finally returned on-chain assets to some creditors.

sources.title: Notice Regarding Repayment in Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash

title: Saxony completes emergency sale of nearly 50,000 BTC
summary: German authorities completed the sale of about 49,858 BTC provisionally secured in the Movie2k criminal case.
details: Saxony's specialized prosecutors sold the assets between June 19 and July 12, mostly over the counter, for about €2.64 billion. The proceeds remained secured for the criminal proceeding and were not immediately ordinary government revenue.
whyItMatters: The market absorbed one of the largest time-bounded government sales of seized bitcoin on record.

sources.title: Emergency Sale of Almost 50,000 Bitcoins Completed

title: Donald Trump proposes retaining U.S.-held Bitcoin
summary: At a Bitcoin conference in Nashville, presidential candidate Donald Trump pledged that a future administration would retain federal bitcoin holdings.
details: The campaign speech also included promises about mining, self-custody, and regulatory leadership. It was a policy proposal at the time, not an executive action or enacted reserve.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin became an explicit national campaign issue and the proposed stockpile later informed federal policy.

sources.title: Former President Trump Speaks at Bitcoin Conference in Nashville

title: Russia enacts a formal cryptocurrency-mining framework
summary: President Vladimir Putin signed Federal Law 221-FZ regulating digital-currency mining and mining-infrastructure operators.
details: The law created registration and reporting obligations for businesses and allowed limited household mining below energy thresholds. It also authorized the government to restrict mining in particular regions or during energy constraints.
whyItMatters: A major mining jurisdiction moved the industry into an explicit national legal and energy-control framework.

title: SEC approves options listing on BlackRock's Bitcoin fund
summary: The SEC approved Nasdaq ISE's rule change to list and trade options on the iShares Bitcoin Trust.
details: The order applied exchange options rules and an initial 25,000-contract position and exercise limit. Other exchanges and Bitcoin funds received related approvals in October.
whyItMatters: A regulated options layer expanded hedging, income, and risk-transfer strategies around spot Bitcoin ETP shares.

sources.title: Order Approving Options on the iShares Bitcoin Trust

title: Options on a U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF begin trading
summary: Nasdaq began trading listed options on BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust after regulatory and clearing approvals.
details: The launch brought standardized calls and puts into the largest spot Bitcoin ETP. Products on additional Bitcoin funds followed on other exchanges over the next several sessions.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin ETP market structure gained the options liquidity and hedging tools common to mature asset classes.

sources.title: Bitcoin ETF Options Market Launch
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission EDGAR

title: Bitcoin trades above $100,000
summary: Bitcoin crossed the $100,000 level on major dollar markets for the first time.
details: The milestone followed strong spot-ETF demand, the fourth halving, and expectations of a more supportive U.S. policy environment. Exact timestamps and highs vary among continuously trading venues.
whyItMatters: A six-figure price became a widely recognized marker of Bitcoin's transition into a large global asset market.

sources.title: Bitcoin Tops $100,000 as Post-Election Rally Continues

title: Microsoft shareholders reject a Bitcoin investment assessment
summary: Microsoft shareholders voted against a proposal asking the board to assess adding bitcoin to the company's balance sheet.
details: The board had recommended a vote against the proposal, saying it already evaluated a range of investable assets. The result did not prohibit Microsoft from considering Bitcoin in the future.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin treasury policy became a formal shareholder-governance question at one of the world's largest companies.
actors: National Center for Public Policy Research

title: MicroStrategy is selected for the Nasdaq-100
summary: Nasdaq announced that MicroStrategy would join the Nasdaq-100 index effective before trading on December 23.
details: The company's market value had become closely linked to its large leveraged Bitcoin treasury strategy. Index inclusion meant passive funds tracking the Nasdaq-100 would acquire exposure to its shares, not bitcoin directly.
whyItMatters: A Bitcoin-treasury company entered one of the world's most tracked large-cap equity indexes.

sources.title: Annual Changes to the Nasdaq-100 Index

title: El Salvador and IMF agree on Bitcoin-policy changes
summary: An IMF staff-level financing agreement called for voluntary private Bitcoin acceptance and reduced public-sector participation.
details: The program contemplated legal reform, dollar-only tax payment, greater transparency, and a gradual government exit from the Chivo wallet. It was a staff-level agreement subject to IMF board approval and domestic implementation.
whyItMatters: El Salvador began a formal retreat from mandatory elements of its original Bitcoin Law without banning private use.

sources.title: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with El Salvador

title: MiCA becomes fully applicable across the EU
summary: The main provisions of the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation began applying after its staged implementation period.
details: Crypto-asset service providers moved toward MiCA authorization, governance, conduct, and prudential requirements. Existing nationally authorized firms could use differing member-state transition periods, in some cases as late as July 1, 2026.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin exchanges and custodians began operating under a common EU-wide legal framework rather than only national regimes.

title: SEC forms a dedicated crypto task force
summary: Acting SEC Chair Mark Uyeda launched an agency task force led by Commissioner Hester Peirce to develop a clearer crypto regulatory framework.
details: The task force was directed to clarify regulatory boundaries, disclosure approaches, registration paths, and enforcement priorities. Its creation did not repeal securities laws or determine the status of every digital asset.
