whyItMatters: The SEC shifted part of its digital-asset agenda from primarily case-by-case enforcement toward a public policy-development process.

sources.title: SEC Crypto 2.0: Acting Chairman Uyeda Announces Formation of New Crypto Task Force

title: SEC staff rescinds SAB 121
summary: Staff Accounting Bulletin 122 removed the SEC staff guidance that had required certain crypto custodians to record safeguarding assets and liabilities at gross fair value.
details: After rescission, companies assess loss-contingency accounting under existing U.S. GAAP or IFRS requirements and continue relevant disclosures. SAB 122 became effective January 30 and permitted retrospective application.
whyItMatters: A widely cited accounting obstacle to bank and public-company Bitcoin custody was removed.

title: United States changes executive-branch digital-asset policy
summary: President Donald Trump signed an order promoting lawful public-blockchain use and creating a presidential working group on digital-asset markets.
details: The order revoked the prior administration's 2022 digital-assets order, opposed a U.S. central-bank digital currency, and directed work on a federal framework. It also asked the group to evaluate a national digital-asset stockpile rather than immediately creating one.
whyItMatters: U.S. executive policy moved toward explicit support for self-custody, mining, open networks, and digital-asset industry growth.
actors: President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets

sources.title: Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology

title: El Salvador makes private Bitcoin acceptance voluntary
summary: El Salvador's assembly amended the Bitcoin Law to remove mandatory private acceptance and limit public-sector involvement.
details: The reform preserved a legal framework for voluntary private Bitcoin transactions but removed core features of the 2021 legal-tender mandate. It also shifted tax payments to U.S. dollars and was enacted as a prior action for the IMF program, with the amended text taking effect on April 30.
whyItMatters: The first country to mandate Bitcoin acceptance formally reversed the compulsory part of its national adoption policy.

sources.title: Amended Bitcoin Law, Legislative Decree No. 57

title: Bybit loses about $1.5 billion in the largest crypto theft on record
summary: Attackers redirected a routine cold-to-hot wallet transfer, taking the largest single haul in the industry's history.
details: The compromise reached a developer machine at the multi-signature wallet provider Safe, letting the attackers present a malicious transaction that looked legitimate to signers. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's Lazarus Group, and the proceeds were laundered within days.
whyItMatters: The largest theft in the market's history came through the signing workflow rather than the chain, and funded a sanctioned state weapons programme.
technicalNote: The stolen assets were predominantly ether rather than bitcoin, but much of the value was converted into bitcoin during laundering.

sources.title: North Korea Responsible for $1.5 Billion Bybit Hack

title: United States establishes a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
summary: President Donald Trump ordered the creation of a reserve capitalized with federally held bitcoin that had been finally forfeited.
details: The order directed that reserve bitcoin should not be sold and required agencies to account for government digital assets. It allowed Treasury and Commerce to develop budget-neutral acquisition strategies, but it did not authorize unrestricted taxpayer-funded purchases or set a purchase schedule.
whyItMatters: Bitcoin became a named strategic reserve asset of the U.S. federal government rather than only seized property awaiting disposal.

title: OCC removes its crypto supervisory non-objection process
summary: OCC Interpretive Letter 1183 reaffirmed permissible bank crypto activities while rescinding the prior requirement for written supervisory non-objection.
details: The letter retained the legal conclusions on custody, certain stablecoin activities, and distributed-ledger payment operations. Banks remained responsible for safe and sound risk management and compliance under ordinary supervision.
whyItMatters: Federally chartered banks could approach Bitcoin custody without a separate pre-clearance step unique to the activity.
actors: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

title: BlackRock's first European Bitcoin ETP begins trading
summary: The iShares Bitcoin ETP listed on Xetra and Euronext exchanges as a physically backed European product.
details: The security referenced the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate and used Coinbase Luxembourg as custodian. It was a debt security under a crypto-linked securities program rather than a UCITS fund.
whyItMatters: BlackRock extended its spot Bitcoin product strategy from the United States into multiple European markets.

title: New Hampshire authorizes limited public-fund Bitcoin investment
summary: Governor Kelly Ayotte signed HB 302, allowing the state treasurer to invest up to five percent of specified funds in qualifying digital assets and precious metals.
details: A digital asset had to average more than $500 billion in market capitalization over the prior calendar year, a threshold Bitcoin alone met when the law passed. The law authorized investment but did not require a purchase or confirm that bitcoin had already been acquired.
whyItMatters: New Hampshire became the first U.S. state to explicitly authorize direct Bitcoin investment from designated public funds.

title: Coinbase discloses an insider-assisted data theft
summary: Coinbase reported that criminals bribed overseas support personnel to obtain data used in social-engineering attacks and extortion.
details: The incident exposed information for a subset of customers but did not compromise passwords, private keys, or Coinbase-controlled customer funds. Coinbase rejected a $20 million demand, planned eligible reimbursements, and initially estimated $180 million to $400 million in related expenses.
whyItMatters: The breach showed that identity and support-system compromise can endanger Bitcoin users even when cryptographic keys remain secure.

title: Texas establishes a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
summary: Texas SB 21 took effect after the governor signed legislation creating a special reserve outside the state treasury.
details: The comptroller may acquire qualifying cryptocurrencies with a market capitalization of at least $500 billion, effectively limiting initial eligibility to Bitcoin. The law created governance and custody authority but did not itself specify an immediate purchase amount.
whyItMatters: Texas became the first large U.S. state to create a named, independently administered Bitcoin reserve fund.

title: The CLARITY Act passes the U.S. House
summary: A market-structure bill dividing oversight between the SEC and CFTC passed 294 to 134 with bipartisan support.
details: The bill would give digital assets a statutory test for when they are commodities rather than securities, and assign spot market supervision to the CFTC. It passed during a week of crypto legislation that also sent the GENIUS Act to the president.
whyItMatters: It is the first time either chamber approved a comprehensive framework rather than legislating around the edges.

sources.title: H.R.3633 — Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025

title: United States enacts the GENIUS Act
summary: The GENIUS Act became federal law, creating a regulatory framework for permitted payment stablecoin issuers.
details: The law addressed reserve assets, redemption, disclosures, supervision, and the relationship between federal and state issuer regimes. It did not regulate Bitcoin as a stablecoin, but it materially changed the dollar-token infrastructure widely used in Bitcoin markets.
whyItMatters: The United States enacted its first major standalone federal law for a core part of cryptocurrency market infrastructure.

title: Bitcoin reaches its all-time high near $126,000
summary: The price peaked at roughly $126,000, the highest level Bitcoin has traded at.
details: The rally had run on spot ETF inflows, corporate treasury buying and a supportive U.S. policy turn. Four days later the market suffered the largest liquidation event in its history, and the price has not returned to this level since.
whyItMatters: This is the top of the cycle that institutional access built, and the beginning of the drawdown that followed it.
technicalNote: Quoted peaks differ slightly by venue and index; figures near $126,000 are commonly cited for 6 October 2025.

title: Bitcoin Core v30 relaxes the OP_RETURN limit
summary: The release raised the default size of data a node will relay in an OP_RETURN output, splitting the developer community.
details: The default datacarrier size moved from 83 bytes to 100,000, on the argument that the old cap merely pushed data into forms that are worse for the UTXO set. Opponents argued it invited blockchain bloat and legal exposure for node operators, and directed users to Bitcoin Knots, whose share of listening nodes rose above a fifth of the network.
whyItMatters: It is the sharpest split among Bitcoin developers since 2017, and it is about relay policy rather than consensus rules.
technicalNote: This is standardness policy, not a consensus rule. Nodes that keep the old limit remain fully valid and stay on the same chain; they simply decline to relay the larger outputs.

title: The largest liquidation event in crypto history
summary: More than $19 billion of leveraged positions were forcibly closed in twenty-four hours after a tariff announcement.
details: A post announcing 100% tariffs on Chinese imports triggered selling into a market carrying record leverage, and bitcoin fell from roughly $122,000 to $105,000 while smaller tokens lost far more. Exchange infrastructure failed under the load, amplifying the cascade well beyond the initial move.
whyItMatters: It showed how much of the market's price was resting on borrowed money, and it marked the end of the 2025 advance.
technicalNote: Roughly $19.4 billion in liquidations across more than 1.6 million accounts, by far the largest single-day total on record.

sources.title: The biggest crypto wipeout was led not by bitcoin, but much smaller tokens

title: Bitcoin's worst start to a year on record
summary: The price fell below $61,000, more than 50% down from October's high, in the weakest opening fifty days Bitcoin has had.
details: Declines in both January and February had never happened back to back before. Delayed market-structure legislation, doubt about the artificial-intelligence trade, uncertainty over Federal Reserve leadership and a new round of tariffs removed the rate-cut expectations the 2025 rally had been built on.
whyItMatters: The drawdown followed the most favourable policy environment Bitcoin has ever had, which complicates the story that regulation was the constraint.

sources.title: Bitcoin logs worst first 50-day start to a year on record

title: Bitcoin's mined supply passes 20 million BTC
summary: Bitcoin's cumulative issued supply crossed 20 million BTC at block 940,000.
details: Fewer than one million of the 21 million nominal maximum remained to be issued through future subsidies, although issuance will continue for more than a century. Circulating or spendable supply is lower because some coins are provably unspendable or presumed lost.
whyItMatters: More than 95 percent of Bitcoin's programmed maximum supply had been issued while the final portion entered a long declining schedule.

sources.title: Bitcoin's Mined Supply Hits 20 Million Milestone

technicalNote: Scheduled issuance reaches exactly 20,000,000 BTC at block 940,000 (10,500,000 + 5,250,000 + 2,625,000 + 1,312,500 + 100,000 × 3.125). Actual issuance trails the schedule by roughly 200 BTC because some coinbase transactions claimed less than the available subsidy or are unspendable, so the economic crossing came a few dozen blocks later. The figure describes consensus issuance, not spendable supply.

title: Senate Banking advances the CLARITY Act
summary: The committee approved the market-structure bill 15 to 9, sending it toward the full Senate.
details: A dispute over whether stablecoin issuers may pay yield had stalled the bill since January, and several large crypto firms withdrew support over the DeFi and yield provisions. The bill had not been reconciled with the House text or enacted by August 2026.
whyItMatters: The framework the industry spent a decade asking for stalled on a disagreement inside the industry itself.
actors: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

title: U.S. order directs regulators to integrate financial technology
summary: President Donald Trump issued an order directing federal financial regulators to streamline treatment of fintech and digital-asset services.
details: The order covered areas including custody, brokerage, payments, lending, and digital-asset-related bank services. It directed reviews and coordination within existing statutory authority rather than automatically approving every proposed product.
whyItMatters: Digital-asset integration became an explicit cross-regulator objective for the traditional U.S. financial system.

sources.title: Integrating Financial Technology Innovation into Regulatory Frameworks

title: Texas appoints its Bitcoin reserve advisory committee
summary: The Texas comptroller appointed the five-member committee charged with advising on the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve's administration.
details: Members were tasked with recommendations on valuation, risk, asset management, security, and custody. The appointment operationalized governance required by the 2025 law but did not by itself document a bitcoin purchase.
whyItMatters: A state Bitcoin reserve moved from statutory authorization toward permanent administrative infrastructure.
actors: Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Advisory Committee

sources.title: Acting Texas Comptroller Names Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Advisory Committee Members

title: Strategy's premium disappears and it starts selling
summary: The largest corporate holder traded below the value of its own bitcoin and began disposing of coins.
details: Strategy had funded years of purchases by issuing shares above the value of its holdings, a mechanism that stops working once the multiple falls under one. Having built its identity on never selling, the company sold bitcoin several times during 2026 to meet dividend and financing obligations.
whyItMatters: It tested whether the corporate treasury model is a permanent source of demand or a leveraged bet that unwinds, and every company that copied it faces the same arithmetic.
technicalNote: mNAV is the ratio of a company's market value to the value of its bitcoin holdings. Above one, issuing shares to buy bitcoin adds bitcoin per share; below one, it subtracts.

title: Maximum EU MiCA transition period ends
summary: The final EU-wide grandfathering deadline expired for crypto-asset service providers operating under pre-MiCA national law.
details: Member states could choose shorter transition periods, so many firms had faced earlier deadlines. From July 1, any provider still serving EU clients without the required MiCA authorization had to cease covered activity unless another lawful basis applied.
whyItMatters: The European Bitcoin service market completed its move from mixed national transitions to the common MiCA licensing regime.
